speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: During that speech, I shared the acronym L-A-S-T.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Apparently, it was not my last Adjournment Motion.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: But, briefly, "L" stands for Literacy – to include mental health literacy in schoos and workplaces. "A" for Accessibility – to increase accessibility for people to come and seek help easier. "S" for Screening – like how we go for regular physical health screening, there should be one for mental health too.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: And "T" for Time-outs – to allow individuals to take a break and come back recharged.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: PAP Members of Parliament have been championing it in Parliament long before I had.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It dates back to the mental health blueprint in 2007.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: From time to time, PAP Members of Parliament have risen in this House to ensure that policies on mental health are up to date and relevant.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Ground-up campaigns such as Beyond The Label, the Honest Cookie by Samaritans of Singapore and ThisConnect, to name a few, have not gone unnoticed.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Even among our own PAP Members of Parliament, we embarked on our own #452TooMany Campaign last month to bring together our community partners, volunteers and residents to discuss issues on mental health.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Although discussions and engagements are still ongoing, I would like to share some of those findings and recommendations today.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: If we picture a pyramid structure of mental health issues, certainly suicide is at its peak.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: What I want to bring forth today is not just the peak but the different ways we can come together to overcome issues surrounding mental health.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Mental health issues can affect anyone, from children to the elderly, students to teachers, workers to retirees.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Efforts to curtail the spread of the pandemic are necessary but unfortunately, have impacted the mental health of Singaporeans in different magnitudes.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Measures to reduce social gatherings since the pandemic have increased stress and loneliness levels amongst our elderly and youths.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This reduction of meaningful social engagement, coupled with stressors of the pandemic and adapting to technology and HBL, have understandably taken a toll on their mental well-being.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Another group of concern is our local Singaporean workers, our frontline healthcare professionals, teachers and public service officers have seen an increase in workload since the onset of the pandemic.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: At its simplest form, those working from home faced the blurring of lines between work and personal time.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: For example, educators have had to adapt to the fluid COVID-19 situation tailoring their lesson plans and materials at short notice on top of the regular administrative duties, juggling various stakeholders' expectations and putting their students' first, always.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: As an educator I feel overwhelmed, frustrated and of course, worried.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: So, I would like to take this opportunity to thank our teachers for their commitment, their dedication for being our fortress in such turbulent times.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It is about time we change this "Assessment of Learning", culture to a "Journey of Learning".

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: If we can create a culture of appreciating the joy of learning and the challenges that such journey presents be it easy or difficult, whether we succeed or fail in something and accepting that there are multiple paths to achieve success, we can nurture an optimal mental health environment from the onset.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Hopefully, this would lead to a positive effect on the "parent-teacher-child" relationship and the positivity trickle down to our society.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Our Singaporean workers, from healthcare professionals to teachers to public service officers, need our continued care and support.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Therefore, reviewing their workscope may be useful for a quality work life balance, but, most importantly, we must continue to create and upgrade channels for meaningful communication and this does not include the biannual staff appraisal.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Anyone screened for being at risk or having symptoms of mental health issues should promptly be referred to a Mental Health Practitioner.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: We want to engage early, before mental health issues disrupts their lives and risks them doing something harmful.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: By expanding our community mental health touchpoints, we can make mental health screening accessible to more Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: But beyond the hardware, it is the software that matters too.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Diagnosing or sensing mental health issues takes time getting to know the patient, building trust and delving into the situation can make a difference.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Therefore, it could be useful to consider and budget for longer consultation times in the future healthcare system.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The first approach is to review expanding existing programmes or creating equivalent ones in IHLs so that more mental health professionals can be produced.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The second, is to develop a community support network of trained staff and volunteers.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: They can be our first point of contact to attend distress calls and walk in consultations.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Therefore, I welcome the Task force’s recommendation to develop a national mental health competency framework with a common set of training standards and clearly defined degrees of competencies expected of professionals and para professionals.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I hope this framework can be extended to students in IHLs as part of a module, so they too can be a ready-resource for the community support network.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Similarly, I hope the training can also be extended to working professionals to develop their competencies and be their organisation's resource person at work.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Mr Speaker, lastly, I would like to touch on cost.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: For mental health patients seeking help, the financial costs of treatment, especially over a long period, can be prohibitive.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: However, this may be fully used after a few consultations.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The Government could also provide greater subsidies for those who are under the Pioneer or Merdeka Generations, as well as those having CHAS cards.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Although insurance policy providers have started to offer insurance policies that provide coverage for mental health conditions, there are many other providers who have not begun.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Thus, I am heartened to know when Senior Minister of State Janil previously told this House that there are ongoing efforts to make treatment more affordable and MOH is also working with insurance companies and other stakeholders to further optimise the coverage process.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: (In Malay):   Mental health is a very critical issue faced by Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In my English speech earlier, I suggested three broad aspects in our efforts to prioritise mental health in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: First, identify the most vulnerable groups and give them support as soon as possible.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: And third, reducing the cost of mental healthcare.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: So far, many activities and programmes are carried out to enhance awareness on mental health, and I personally support and welcome such efforts.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: However, our journey is still a long one.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: My hope is that with this suggestion, Singaporeans who are suffering from mental health issues are no longer ashamed to come forward to get support, and also view mental health as no less important than physical health.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, I have touched on three broad points as part of our efforts to prioritise mental healthcare and support for Singaporeans: identification, infrastructure and cost.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: We need to focus our efforts on identifying the vulnerable groups so that we can intervene quickly, review our current mental health infrastructure and explore how we can make mental health consultations affordable for those in need.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: We need to take affirmative action now, beyond just performative activism and populist rhetorics.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: To this end, I would like to thank my fellow PAP Members of Parliament colleagues for joining me in the #452TooMany Campaign.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: A special thanks to our community partners, volunteers, residents, mental health practitioners and researchers, like Devan from Mental Act and Jonathan from Total Wellness Initiative, for contributing their ideas and suggestions to strengthen our resolve to support Singapore's mental health movement.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Special mention also goes out to four inspiring individuals: Xavierlyn, Athena, Afiqah and Devan who shared their experiences on mental health issues with me.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I am heartened to hear their sharing and I believe that conversations like these must continue and so that we can destigmatise mental health.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This act of solidarity will not just end here.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I am inviting Members of this House, community leaders, activists, influencers and the public to join me and my 18 Members of Parliament on 10 October in conjunction with World Mental Health Day.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Let us post on our socials, this 10.10 at 10.10 am a message of hope and commitment with the hashtag #452TooMany to signify that we acknowledge and care about mental health in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Mr Speaker, to those out there grappling with mental health, I would like to end with a n online quote that I have adapted: "You are bent but not broken.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: You are depressed but not giving up." We are not giving up and you are not alone.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Not that you need to, given that it is 11.30 pm, just saying.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Member raised three points for our consideration: (a) identify vulnerable groups or persons who are at risk and provide proactive support; (b) review our mental health infrastructure and (c) review of the mental health consultation cost.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I will address these points as I highlight the efforts which the Government has carried out and areas which we continue to build on.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Government adopts a comprehensive and multi-pronged approach towards mental healthcare and support.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The key strategies cover mental health promotion and upstream prevention, early detection and intervention, disease management, care integration and social support across different settings.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Over the years, the Government has been reviewing the range of mental health services and programmes available to the public on a regular basis to ensure that they meet the needs of the population.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In 2007, MOH developed the National Mental Health Blueprint to promote mental health, build resilience and reduce the impact of mental illness.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Under the Blueprint, we began developing community capability, a key shift that entailed moving from an acute-centric institutionalised model to a community-based model.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: While acute care remains an important component of the system, only the acutely ill, disturbed or those with high risk of harm to self or others need to be hospitalised.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For those whose conditions have stabilised, they should be discharged and allowed to recover and reintegrate back into the community.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Community Mental Health (CMH) Masterplan, launched in 2012, builds on the 2007 Blueprint and further strengthens mental health care in the community, to enable persons with mental health needs to be well supported in the community.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Through establishing more community-based services, we hope to facilitate greater acceptance of treatment, lower the stigma of mental illness and increase community outreach for early identification of mental health needs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These national mental health plans have expanded the community touch-points to promptly identify and assess at-risk persons with mental health needs and link them to relevant services.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These efforts will address the Member’s concerns of ensuring that those who are most vulnerable or at-risk are identified early and interventions are in place to protect them from doing something harmful.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Member had also called for an expansion of the infrastructure by equipping all polyclinics, General Practitioners and social service agencies with the necessary expertise and resources.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In this regard, I would highlight that under the CMH Masterplan, we have also increased the accessibility of mental health services in primary and community care sectors.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: They are supported in the community by our 21 community intervention teams, which comprise trained allied health professionals to provide psycho-social therapeutic interventions.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MOH will continue to work with the healthcare providers and social services agencies to expand and improve mental health services in the primary and community care settings, including training of frontline staff and community partners.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Member also raised the issue of cost.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MOH has put in place various support measures to ensure access to affordable mental health services.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Government provides up to 75% subsidies for outpatient treatment at polyclinics and public specialist outpatient clinics (SOCs).

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: All Singaporeans regardless of income are also eligible for subsidies under the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) for treatment of mental health conditions under the Chronic Disease Management Programme (CDMP) at participating private General Practitioner (GP) clinics.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Pioneer and Merdeka Generation cardholders are eligible for additional subsidies at all polyclinics, public SOCs and CHAS GP clinics.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Patients can also tap on their MediSave to pay for outpatient treatment of CDMP conditions.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Nevertheless, in recognition that patients with complex conditions may have higher needs, we increased the MediSave withdrawal limit to $700 for patients with complex chronic conditions in January 2021, in recognition that these patients have higher needs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The withdrawal limit for patients with simple chronic conditions remain at $500.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Those who are 60 years old and above can additionally tap on the Flexi-MediSave scheme for outpatient expenses.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Flexi-MediSave annual withdrawal limit was also raised from $200 to $300 in June 2021.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To ensure that no Singaporean is denied access to appropriate treatment due to inability to pay, MediFund is available at public healthcare institutions as a safety net to assist Singaporeans who are unable to afford their mental health treatments despite Government subsidies, insurance and MediSave.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MOH will continue to review the various financial schemes regularly to ensure that they meet the needs of Singaporeans with mental health needs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Besides targeting the general population, many of these initiatives are targeted at specific population segments such as parents and families; children and youth; workplaces and working population; and seniors.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It is indeed important for us to create awareness on these issues, or as the Member puts it, to enhance mental health literacy, in our community.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The COVID-19 Mental Wellness Task force (CoMWT), co-chaired by MOH and the Institute of Mental Health (IMH), was set up to address the psychosocial impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the population.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The task force has completed its work and announced its findings and recommendations.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: More details can be found in the task force report which has been published on the MOH website.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The task force will engage the public on the development of this strategy through a public consultation exercise next year.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Notwithstanding the efforts by the Government and agencies, a whole of society approach is necessary to address the population’s mental well-being.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Every one of us has a role to play.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We can start by learning more about mental health and how we could support other in dealing with mental health challenges, reach out and do regular check-ins on the people we care about, and most importantly, practice self-care.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For example, to better reach out to youths, the Government has launched the Youth Mental Well-being Network in February 2020 to bring together the wider society to identify opportunities and gaps to work on to improve youth mental well-being.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To date, there are over 1,500 passionate like-minded individuals including mental health professionals, practitioners, parents and youths in this Network.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The network members have been working on over 20 projects to support youth mental health, ranging from enhancing youths’ emotional resilience to strengthening support among peers, and within the family, workplace and community.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We look forward to seeing the fruits of their labour.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will factor these findings into the work of the Taskforce and its supporting workgroups.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: On this note, I urge my fellow Singaporeans to stand together and support one another, to ensure mental well-being and resilience especially in such unprecedented times.
